title: Planning skill defaults — write phases first, assign their model last, and read the repository's own architecture

ground.note: "Choosing a model and effort" opens with "The default phase model is `claude-opus-5-5`" and keeps Sonnet 5.5 for mechanical phases. "Planning doctrine" states one layer chain (page → view-model → command → domain → port → adapter → storage). "Test strategy (informational)" maps tests to that chain's layers. "Boundary contracts (informational)" lists its boundaries. "Planning constraints" keeps "Comprehensive instructions". "Headless authoring" lists a phase's keys with `model` and `effort` first.

Renders the model-catalog table from DEFAULT_PROVIDER_CONFIG between the `BEGIN generated: model-catalog` markers of the planning skill. `pnpm check:full` runs it with `--check` and fails on drift. The prose above the table is hand-written.
The six skills `phax skills install` exposes, phax-planning among them, each shipped as its SKILL.md.

A plan-document phase spreads the extracted fields (`id`, `model`, `effort`, `planMarkdownAnchor`, planned files, `commit`) first, then the content fields (`title`, `objective`, `detailedInstructions`, …). Every key is required. The preamble already carries `technicalArbitrations`.
The headless prompt is the skill text verbatim, then the output contract, then the document JSON Schema, then the source spec and the brief. It says nothing about the repository's providers.

Spawns the headless session with the `authoring.plan` model and effort (or `--model`/`--effort`), under the review security policy: write access to `.phax-context/` only, provider-only network, and `git` as the only agent command.

`phax brief [path…]` reads its config from the main checkout, so `phax.local.json` serves a phase worktree too. With no provider it prints `✗ No brief provider is configured: add "brief": …` and exits 1. A config error exits 2, and a refusal or a failed provider exits 1.

Builds the brief request (paths relative to the working-tree root, deduplicated, never checked for existence, refused outside the tree), runs the provider from the tree root, and records a pull made inside a phase as `brief-NN.json`.
Runs the provider with no shell, writes the stamped request on its stdin, and has a fixed 60 s limit. It reads the answer by its own `$schema`, and every failure becomes a one-line reason.
The `brief-request` (`$schema` plus phase facts plus `files`, or `$schema` plus `files` outside a phase) and the `brief-record`.

`brief: { command, push }` is accepted in `phax.json` and in the user overlay. `authoring.plan` defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at `high`. `DEFAULT_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_MODEL` is already `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
The config layers: `phax.json`, `phax.local.json` beside it, and `~/.phax/config.json`.
Inside a phase worktree, every registered command must be classified. `brief` and the read-only commands are allowed, and an unclassified command is refused.
Every format has an id in FORMAT_IDS and a `$schema` URL `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format-id>/<X.Y.Z>.json`. New formats join SCHEMA_BORN_FORMAT_IDS.
Each format's current shape is snapshotted as `next.schema.json` and renamed to the release at the cut. The manifests name the opened version (0.25.0 today).
Draft. Adds the optional `phax.planning.json` and its lint, and also reorders the plan document and sets the Sonnet default. It is to be reworked to build on this spec.
Every provider request and answer carries `$schema`. phax stays autonomous. "The brief at plan authoring" is still unspecced.

context:
The phax-planning skill is what both an interactive planner and a headless plan authoring session read: phax ships it, `phax skills install` copies it, and the headless prompt opens with it verbatim. Its "Choosing a model and effort" section starts from the strongest tier: "The default phase model is `claude-opus-5-5`: it is the cheapest Opus-tier entry and matches or beats `claude-fable-5-1` from `medium` effort up". It keeps `claude-sonnet-5-5` for mechanical phases. The section sits above the generated model-catalog table, but its own prose is hand-written. So a catalog change regenerates the table and can leave the prose naming a model the table no longer lists.

The skill also has the planner pick each phase's model before writing the phase. The plan document a headless planner returns lists `id`, `model` and `effort` first among a phase's keys, before `title`, `objective` and the instructions. A model writes JSON in key order, so it commits to a model before it has written what the model must do. The planner's own model is separate: it comes from `authoring.plan` (default `claude-opus-5-5` at `high`) or from `--model`/`--effort`.

The skill states one architecture as doctrine. "Planning doctrine" traces every need through page → view-model → command → domain → port → adapter → storage and orders the work domain → ports → command → adapter → view-model → view → route. "Test strategy" maps test types to those layers, and "Boundary contracts" names their boundaries.

Providers reach phax as commands declared in `phax.json`. `phax brief [path…]` is the model for a pull. It reads `brief` from the config layers (`phax.json`, `phax.local.json`, `~/.phax/config.json`) of the main checkout. It writes a `$schema`-stamped request on the provider's stdin, has a fixed 60 s limit, and reads a `$schema`-stamped answer. The phase guard allows it inside a phase worktree. With no provider it exits 1. The headless authoring session runs under the review security policy: it may write only `.phax-context/`, has provider-only network, and may run `git` and nothing else.

An experiment outside phax took one ticket and a two-phase plan written once by the headless planner. It executed that plan 24 times with `phax run`, choosing every phase's model itself. On the plan as written, every run at Sonnet 5.5 (half Opus 5.5's cost) and at Haiku 5.5 (a sixth) delivered the ticket and kept the codebase's rules. The one run that broke a rule ran at Opus. With the plan's detailed instructions removed, Haiku broke a rule in two runs of three without a guarantee gate and in none with one. The strong planner's plan carried most of the work, as the planner/executor and architect/editor splits of published practice predict. The author decided the three changes below on 2026-10-17.
problem:
phax spends the strongest tier on every phase by default, although a plan written by a strong planner carried lighter executors at a half or a sixth of the cost. The planner also chooses in the wrong order: it picks a model, then writes instructions for it, instead of choosing from what the written phase asks for. In headless authoring, the document's key order forces that wrong order. The default is named in hand-written prose beside a generated catalog, so the next catalog change can leave it pointing at a stale model.

The skill hands every repository one architecture as if it were the planner's doctrine. A repository built otherwise (no view-model, no ports, a different test pyramid) gets phases traced through layers it does not have, with tests mapped to layers that do not exist. The repository's own architecture is the one that should shape the plan. phax has no seam through which a provider that knows that architecture can say so, and the planner is never told where to look for it.

productGoal.statement: The planner writes each phase first. It then gives the phase a model and effort from what the written phase asks for, starting from `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`. It goes stronger only where the phase must design what the code does not show yet, and lighter where it reproduces a pattern a gate checks, and every departure says why. The skill keeps its planning principle as doctrine and treats its layer chain as one example. The planner reads the repository's own architecture from a provider through `phax architecture` when one is configured, and from the code and its documentation otherwise. A missing provider is information, not a failure.
productGoal.guidingRule: The plan is written by a strong planner against the repository's own architecture; the executor's model is chosen last, from the written phase, and phax never chooses or rewrites it.

terminology.definition: The model and effort the skill tells the planner to give a phase unless the phase calls for another: `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`. It is guidance to the planner. phax never applies it to a phase.
A phase whose model or effort differs from the default phase assignment. Every departure carries its reason.
The skill's rules for choosing a phase's model and effort: the default phase assignment, when to go stronger, when to go lighter, and the reason a departure must carry.
The skill's layer chain, test-strategy layer table and boundary list, presented as one possible shape of a repository, not as the planner's doctrine.
Plan outside-in, implement inside-out, verify outside-in, stated without naming any layer.
A command declared as `architecture` in a config layer. phax writes an architecture request on its stdin and reads an architecture report from its stdout.
The `$schema`-stamped document phax sends the architecture provider: `files`, null for the whole repository or the requested paths.
The `$schema`-stamped document the architecture provider prints: a Markdown `body` for the agent to read, and nothing else.

requirements.title: Phases are written before they are assigned
requirements.statement: The phax-planning skill shall tell the planner to cut and write every phase before choosing that phase's model and effort from what the written phase asks for.

requirements.title: The plan document puts the assignment last
requirements.statement: The plan document JSON Schema shall place each phase's `model` and `effort` after every other key of the phase.

requirements.title: Existing sidecars still read
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reads a plan sidecar written before the reordering THE system SHALL decode it with the same phases, models and efforts as before.

requirements.title: Sonnet at medium is the default
requirements.statement: The skill's model policy shall name `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium` as the default phase assignment and shall no longer name `claude-opus-5-5` as the default phase model.

requirements.title: Stronger where the phase designs something new
requirements.statement: The skill's model policy shall direct a higher effort, or `claude-opus-5-5`, for a phase that must design something no code in the repository shows yet, such as a new state machine, an adapter to a system the code does not reach yet, or a choice that crosses several parts of the architecture.

requirements.title: Lighter where a pattern exists and a gate checks it
requirements.statement: The skill's model policy shall direct `claude-haiku-5-5` for a phase that reproduces a pattern the repository's code already holds and that a configured gate checks.

requirements.title: Every departure says why
requirements.statement: The skill's model policy shall require every departure to state its reason, on the phase or in Technical arbitrations.

requirements.title: Headless departures are reasoned in the preamble
requirements.statement: The skill's Headless authoring section shall direct the reason of each departure into `preamble.technicalArbitrations`, as one entry naming the phase id, its model and effort, and why.

requirements.title: Detailed instructions stay
requirements.statement: The skill shall keep its "Comprehensive instructions" planning constraint.

requirements.title: The planner's own model is unchanged
requirements.statement: The system shall spawn headless plan authoring with the model and effort from `--model`/`--effort`, else `authoring.plan`, else the built-in authoring default, as before this spec.

requirements.title: phax never rewrites a stated model
requirements.statement: The system shall render, extract and run each phase with exactly the model and effort the planner stated, never substituting the default phase assignment.

requirements.title: The policy's model names follow the catalog
requirements.statement: IF the skill's model-policy text differs from the text phax generates from its default phase assignment and the policy's named models THEN `pnpm check:full` SHALL fail.

requirements.title: The policy names only catalog entries
requirements.statement: IF a model or effort that the skill's model policy names is absent from the shipped catalog THEN `pnpm check:full` SHALL fail, naming that model or effort.

requirements.title: The planning principle stays doctrine
requirements.statement: The skill's Planning doctrine shall state plan outside-in, implement inside-out and verify outside-in without naming any layer.

requirements.title: The layer chain is an example
requirements.statement: The skill shall present the layer chain, the test-strategy layer table and the boundary-contract list as one example architecture, to use only where the repository's own architecture matches it.

requirements.title: Where the repository's architecture comes from
requirements.statement: The skill shall tell the planner to read the repository's architecture before cutting phases: from `phax architecture` when an architecture provider is configured, and otherwise from the code and its documentation (README, CLAUDE.md or equivalent).

requirements.title: The architecture provider is configured like brief
requirements.statement: WHERE `architecture` is declared in `phax.json`, `phax.local.json` or `~/.phax/config.json` THE system SHALL use its `command` as the architecture provider, merged across layers as `brief` is.

requirements.title: No path asks for the whole repository
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax architecture` runs with no path and an architecture provider is configured THE system SHALL send the provider an architecture request whose `files` is null and print the body of its architecture report.

requirements.title: Paths ask for the parts that hold them
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax architecture <path>...` runs and an architecture provider is configured THE system SHALL send the provider an architecture request whose `files` lists the paths, relative to the working-tree root, deduplicated, in the order given and never checked for existence, and print the body of its architecture report.

requirements.title: Paths outside the working tree are refused
requirements.statement: IF a path given to `phax architecture` resolves outside the working tree THEN the system SHALL exit 1 naming the path, without running the provider.

requirements.title: The request and the report are phax formats
requirements.statement: The system shall stamp the architecture request and read the architecture report by their `$schema` URLs, as the formats `architecture-request` and `architecture-report`, and publish both JSON Schemas with every phax format.

requirements.title: A failed provider is one line and exit 1
requirements.statement: IF the architecture provider exits non-zero, outruns its time limit, or prints anything that does not decode as an architecture report THEN `phax architecture` SHALL print one line naming the architecture provider and the reason, and exit 1.

requirements.title: No provider is information
requirements.statement: IF no architecture provider is configured THEN `phax architecture` SHALL print, on stdout, one line saying none is configured and to read the architecture from the code and its documentation (README, CLAUDE.md or equivalent), and exit 0.

requirements.title: phax brief keeps its exit
requirements.statement: IF no brief provider is configured THEN `phax brief` SHALL keep its current message and exit 1.

requirements.title: Allowed inside a phase worktree
requirements.statement: WHILE the current directory is inside a phase worktree THE system SHALL run `phax architecture` as it runs outside one, reading the config of the repository's main checkout.

requirements.title: A pull leaves no trace
requirements.statement: The system shall write no file when `phax architecture` runs, inside or outside a phase worktree.

requirements.title: The planner is told a provider exists
requirements.statement: WHERE an architecture provider is configured THE system SHALL state in the headless plan authoring prompt that one is configured and that the planner runs `phax architecture`, with no path or with the paths the plan touches, before cutting phases.

requirements.title: The planner is told none exists
requirements.statement: WHERE no architecture provider is configured THE system SHALL state in the headless plan authoring prompt that none is configured and that the planner reads the architecture from the code and its documentation instead.

requirements.title: The headless planner may run the command
requirements.statement: WHERE an architecture provider is configured THE system SHALL allow the headless plan authoring session to run `phax architecture`.

surface.before:
### Choosing a model and effort

- The default phase model is `claude-opus-5-5`: it is the cheapest Opus-tier entry and matches or beats `claude-fable-5-1` from `medium` effort up.
- Use `claude-sonnet-5-5` for mechanical phases (catalog/table edits, renames, doc sweeps).
- Use `claude-fable-5-1` only for a stated reason that Opus 5.5 cannot serve, and record that reason in Technical arbitrations.
- Use the lowest effort that succeeds. Opus 5.5 is weakest at `low` (below Fable 5.1), so use `medium` or above for phases that need real reasoning.
- A plan that changes the catalog itself must name only models already in the shipped catalog: …
surface.after:
### Choosing a model and effort

Cut and write every phase first. Choose its model and effort last, from what the written phase asks for.

<!-- BEGIN generated: phase-model-policy -->
- Default: `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`.
- Stronger (a higher effort, or `claude-opus-5-5`): the phase must design something no code in the repository shows yet — a new state machine, an adapter to a system the code does not reach yet, a choice that crosses several parts of the architecture.
- Lighter (`claude-haiku-5-5`): the phase reproduces a pattern the code already holds, and a configured gate checks it.
<!-- END generated: phase-model-policy -->

- Any other catalog model only for a stated reason.
- Every phase that leaves the default says why: on the phase, or in Technical arbitrations (headless: one `technicalArbitrations` entry naming the phase).
- A lighter model needs the detail: see "Comprehensive instructions".
- A plan that changes the catalog itself must name only models already in the shipped catalog: …

Normative: the order (write, then assign); the default `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`; the stronger and lighter cases and their models; a reason for every departure; the model names generated, not hand-written (per Q1). Indicative: the wording, the marker name, and the placement of the generated block.

surface.after:
## Planning doctrine

- **Plan outside-in.** Start from the need the consumer sees and trace the path it takes through the repository's parts. This is how you discover which files each phase touches.
- **Implement inside-out.** Order the work from the parts others depend on to the surface, so the surface never claims a behavior the core does not yet provide.
- **Verify outside-in.** End by checking the consumer-visible behavior end to end, then let the gates confirm it.

### The repository's architecture

Read it before cutting phases. Run `phax architecture` (or `phax architecture <path>...`): with a provider configured it prints the architecture, and without one it says so in one line. Otherwise read the code and its documentation (README, CLAUDE.md or equivalent).

### One example architecture

A layered application: page → view-model → command → domain → port → adapter → storage, implemented domain → ports → command → adapter → view-model → view → route. Use it only where the repository is built this way.

## Test strategy (informational)

Map tests to the parts of the repository's architecture and pick the cheapest reliable test for each. For the example architecture:
| Layer | Preferred test type | …   (table unchanged)

## Boundary contracts (informational)

When a phase crosses a boundary of the repository's architecture (in the example: page/cli/surface → view-model, …), …

Normative: no layer named in the doctrine bullets; the chain, the table and the boundary list marked as the example; the two sources of the repository's architecture. Indicative: headings and wording.

nonGoals: The optional planning file `phax.planning.json`, its sync and its lint, and any lint check of the default or of departure reasons: the `phase-model-assignment` spec.

What a provider puts in an architecture report beyond a Markdown body: parts, guarantees, dependency order, or any structure phax would read.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a configured provider that exits 3, then one that prints `{"body": "x"}` with no `$schema`, then one that sleeps past the time limit
acceptanceCriteria.then: each run prints one line naming the architecture provider and the reason (the exit code, the missing `$schema` naming the architecture-report URL, the time limit) and exits 1

acceptanceCriteria.name: No provider is information
acceptanceCriteria.given: no `architecture` key in any config layer
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout holds exactly one line saying no architecture provider is configured and naming the code and its documentation (README, CLAUDE.md) as where to read the architecture, stderr is empty, and the exit is 0

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax brief still exits 1 without a provider
acceptanceCriteria.given: no `brief` key in any config layer
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints `✗ No brief provider is configured: …` and exits 1, as before this spec

acceptanceCriteria.name: Allowed in a phase worktree, with no trace
acceptanceCriteria.given: a phase worktree (a linked worktree whose root holds `.phax-context/`) of a repository whose `phax.local.json` declares a fake architecture provider
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax architecture src/core` runs from inside it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the phase guard lets it run, the provider's body is printed with exit 0, and the worktree and the run folder hold no new or changed file

acceptanceCriteria.name: The prompt says a provider is configured
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax artifact new plan invoice-totals --headless --brief brief.md` writes the session's `prompt.md`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the prompt states that an architecture provider is configured and that the planner runs `phax architecture` before cutting phases

acceptanceCriteria.name: The prompt says none is configured
acceptanceCriteria.given: no `architecture` key in any config layer
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax artifact new plan invoice-totals --headless --brief brief.md` writes the session's `prompt.md`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the prompt states that no architecture provider is configured and that the planner reads the code and its documentation instead, and it does not ask the planner to run `phax architecture`

acceptanceCriteria.name: The headless planner may run the command
acceptanceCriteria.given: `architecture` declared in `phax.json` and a secure security profile
acceptanceCriteria.when: headless plan authoring spawns its session
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session's agent commands admit `phax architecture`, and with no `architecture` key they are the same as before this spec

openQuestions.question: How does the skill name the default phase assignment and the policy's models, so that a catalog change cannot leave them stale?

options.label: A generated block in the skill, rendered from one phax constant (default model and effort, stronger and lighter models), with the constant checked against the catalog by the existing `gen:model-catalog --check` step of `pnpm check:full`
options.abandons: Hand-editable prose: changing the default means changing code and regenerating, and the default becomes a phax constant that the later `phase-model-assignment` built-in default must reuse rather than restate.

options.label: Hand-written prose naming the ids, plus a test that every model id the prose names is in the catalog
options.abandons: Catching a stale default: when a newer Sonnet joins and the old one stays listed, the prose still passes while pointing at the older model.

options.label: Name families, not ids ("the newest active claude-sonnet entry")
options.abandons: A concrete id the planner can copy: each planner resolves the family to an id itself, two planners can pick differently, and a non-Claude catalog has no "sonnet".

openQuestions.rationale: The catalog table is already generated and drift-checked in `pnpm check:full`. Putting the policy's model names behind the same mechanism makes the catalog the single source of truth. A hand edit or a missing model then fails the check instead of shipping. The cost is a constant in code, which `phase-model-assignment` needs anyway for its built-in default.

openQuestions.question: Where does a headless phase that leaves the default state why?

options.label: In `preamble.technicalArbitrations`, one entry per departing phase naming its id, model and effort, and the reason
options.abandons: A checkable link: nothing mechanical tells a departure without a reason from one with, and the reason is written away from its phase.

options.label: A new required per-phase key `modelReason` (a string, or null on the default), placed before `model`
options.abandons: Shape stability ahead of `phase-model-assignment`, which will replace it with its `assignment` block: two plan-document shape changes in a row for one concern.

openQuestions.rationale: This spec steers the planner, and lint does not check the reason (that is `phase-model-assignment`'s job, with its own per-phase block). The preamble already holds cross-phase decisions and is required. Adding a field now that the next spec replaces would churn a persisted format for no check that reads it.

openQuestions.question: How does the headless planner reach the architecture?

options.label: Pull: the prompt says whether a provider is configured, and the session may run `phax architecture` when one is
options.abandons: The authoring session's narrow jail: today it runs only `git`. It now runs a command that spawns a provider inside the session's read-only filesystem and provider-only network, which a provider that writes a cache or reaches the network will not survive.

options.label: Push: phax queries the provider once, for the whole repository, before spawning the session, and puts the body in the prompt
options.abandons: Asking for the parts the plan touches: the planner gets one whole-repository answer it cannot narrow. The prompt grows by that answer for every plan, and this departs from the author's stated design.

openQuestions.rationale: The author chose pull. It keeps one path to the architecture for interactive planners, headless planners and phases, and lets the planner ask about the parts it is cutting. The jail's limits are a constraint for the provider to meet, stated in the docs page. `phase-model-assignment` widens the same session for `phax brief` on the same terms.

openQuestions.question: Do `phax brief` and `phax architecture` answer a missing provider the same way?

options.label: `phax architecture` exits 0 with one stdout line; `phax brief` keeps its exit 1
options.abandons: Consistency between two sibling provider commands: the same situation answers 0 from one and 1 from the other.

options.label: Both exit 0 with one stdout line
options.abandons: `phax brief`'s shipped contract before the CLI freeze: a script, gate step or test that reads exit 1 as "no brief provider" starts reading success instead.

options.label: Both exit 1
options.abandons: The author's rule for `phax architecture`: an agent reads exit 1 as a failure and retries or stops, although a missing architecture provider is an ordinary repository.

openQuestions.rationale: The two commands' callers differ. The skill tells a planner to run `phax architecture` in every repository, so a missing provider there is ordinary and must read as information. A phase is told to run `phax brief` only when the project configures a brief provider, so a missing one there is a misconfiguration worth a non-zero exit. Changing brief's exit would also spend CLI-contract churn just before the freeze for no caller's benefit.

openQuestions.question: Is a `phax architecture` call inside a phase worktree recorded, as a pulled brief is?

options.label: Not recorded: nothing is written
options.abandons: The trace of which architecture a phase agent read, which a reviewer could otherwise replay from the phase folder.

options.label: Recorded as `architecture-NN.json` beside the brief records, with a new `architecture-record` format
options.abandons: Minimality of the seam: a third format to version and snapshot, and the brief's collect-and-close machinery duplicated, before any provider says more than a Markdown body.

openQuestions.rationale: The brief asks for the minimal seam. An architecture report informs the plan rather than a phase's compliance, so nothing downstream reads it, and a record format can be added if a consumer appears.

openQuestions.question: What shape is the architecture report?

options.label: `{ $schema, body }`: one Markdown string phax prints and never parses
options.abandons: Anything phax could compute from the answer, such as the parts, their paths or their dependency order: a later consumer must parse prose or wait for a new shape.

options.label: `{ $schema, parts: [{ name, paths, guarantees }], order }`
options.abandons: A seam that exists before any provider says much: every provider must compute parts and an order up front, and phax freezes a structure no consumer reads yet.

openQuestions.rationale: The only reader today is an agent, which reads Markdown best. Adding structure later is a new shape under the versioned-format rules. Requiring it now would force providers to compute what nobody consumes.

settled: The default phase assignment is `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`. Stronger means a higher effort or `claude-opus-5-5` for a phase that designs what the code does not show yet. Lighter means `claude-haiku-5-5` for a phase that reproduces an existing pattern a gate checks. Every departure states its reason.
The planner's own model and `authoring.plan` are untouched. The spec changes what the planner assigns, not the planner.
The plan document's phase keeps its key set. Only `model` and `effort` move to the end. The extracted projection, `phax-plan.json` and the rendered Markdown position of the model lines are unchanged.
The planning principle stays doctrine. The layer chain, the test table and the boundary list become one example architecture.
`phax architecture [path]...` follows `phax brief`: config from the main checkout's layers, stdin request, `$schema`-read answer, no shell, allowed by the phase guard, exit 2 on a config error.
Two new schema-born formats, `architecture-request` (`$schema`, `files`) and `architecture-report` (`$schema`, `body`), are snapshotted and published like every format.
Resolved recommendations: Q1 generated block, Q2 Technical arbitrations, Q3 pull with a grant, Q4 split exits, Q5 no record, Q6 body only.
open: Whether moving `model` and `effort` to the end changes the plan-document snapshot. If it does, decide whether the change rides the format's current `next` snapshot (plan-document was already changed this cycle) or needs a frozen copy and a lift for sidecars stamped earlier.
The architecture provider's time limit: reuse the brief's fixed 60 s, or another fixed value (not a config key).

How the headless session's grant is expressed (a narrow `phax architecture` allowance), and what the session's read jail must admit for phax to read `~/.phax/config.json` and `phax.local.json` and run the provider.
The exact wording of the no-provider line, the failure lines, the prompt statements and the skill's new text.
The name of the generated skill block and whether the existing catalog generator renders it or a sibling does.
constraints: No back-compat shims in persisted schemas: both new formats are born with a required `$schema`, every key is required, and unknown keys are refused.
Explicit per-variant enums: the request's `files` is null or a non-empty list, with no third form.

Respect the layers: the provider is spawned through the Shell port and its config read through the existing loader. Building the request and choosing the prompt statement are pure domain. The report is decoded through a schema at the boundary. The CLI command holds no logic.
phax stays autonomous: a missing or failing architecture provider never stops authoring or a phase, and nothing waits on a person.
phax never chooses or rewrites a model silently: the default is guidance in the skill, and no step substitutes it for a stated model.
`phase-model-assignment` overlaps this spec on the reorder and the default (its §5.1, §5.3). Plan this spec first, and rework that spec to build on it rather than restate it.
The new command must be classified in the phase guard, or the guard's own test refuses it.
Fixtures and examples are made up (`acme-guard`, `acme-billing`, `src/core/billing/totals.ts`).
Tests hold across a release cut: assert `$schema` URLs by format id and the release pattern, never by the running version.

docsPage.reader: A repository owner who wants phax planners to plan against their repository's own architecture, and the author of a provider (such as steme) who wants to supply it.
docsPage.example: Declare `"architecture": { "command": "acme-guard architecture" }` in `phax.json`. Run `phax architecture` and `phax architecture src/core` and see the provider's Markdown body. Read the architecture-request on the provider's stdin and the minimal architecture-report it must print. Remove the key and see the one-line "none configured" answer with exit 0. Note the limits a provider runs under inside a headless planning session (read-only filesystem, provider-only network).
